I can see all three bugs clearly: 1. **parser.ts**: Uses `JSON.stringify` instead of `JSON.parse` — should return the parsed object, not re-stringify it. 2. **filter.ts**: Checks `item.isActive` (camelCase) but test data uses `active` (lowercase). 3. **formatter.ts**: Joins with ` | ` but the test expects `, `. **Fix 1 — parser.ts:**Parser fixed. Two remaining failures — both trace back to `filterActive` returning `[]` because it checks `isActive` while the data uses `active`. **Fix 2 — filter.ts:**Filter fixed. Last failure: `formatOutput` joins with ` | ` but test expects `, `. **Fix 3 — formatter.ts:**All 3 tests pass. Here's a summary of the three bugs fixed: | # | File | Bug | Fix | |---|------|-----|-----| | 1 | `src/parser.ts` | `JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(input))` re-serialized the parsed object to a string, so `parseJSON('[1,2]')` returned `"[1,2]"` instead of `[1,2]`. | Changed to `JSON.parse(input)` — just parse and return the object. | | 2 | `src/filter.ts` | Checked `item.isActive` (camelCase), but the test data uses the key `active` (lowercase), so every item evaluated to falsy and the filter returned `[]`. | Changed to `item.active`. | | 3 | `src/formatter.ts` | Joined IDs with `' | '`, producing `
1 \| 3
`, but the test expects comma-separated: `
1, 3
`. | Changed the joiner to `', '`. |
